question.problem: Given the curve $r(t)=t\,i+(16+{t}^{3})\,j$, find all points at which ${r}^{′}(t)$ and $r(t)$ are parallel.
question.worked_solution:
First, we calculate the derivative of $r(t):$  

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(16+{t}^{3})\,j \\  & =\,i+3{t}^{2}\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

The vectors ${r}^{′}(t)$ and $r(t)$ are parallel for some specific value ${t}_{0}$ of the parameter $t$ if and only if there exists a constant $c$ such that $r({t}_{0})=c\,{r}^{′}({t}_{0}).$ So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =c\,{r}^{′}(t) \\ t\,i+(16+{t}^{3})\,j & =c(i+3{t}^{2}\,j).\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the coefficients of $i,$ and $j$ gives:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}t=c \\ 16+{t}^{3}=c(3{t}^{2})\end{aligned}
$$

From the first equation we obtain $t=c.$ Substituting $c=t$ into the second equality, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}16+{t}^{3} & =3{t}^{3} \\ 16 & =2{t}^{3} \\ t & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $r$ and ${r}^{′}$ are parallel only at the point corresponding to $t=2.$

Finally, since

$$
\begin{aligned}r(2) & =2\,i+(16+{2}^{3})\,j \\  & =2\,i+24\,j,\end{aligned}
$$

we conclude that $r(t)$ and ${r}^{′}(t)$ are parallel at the point $P(2,24).$
